        let view = v_flex()
            .id("file-view")
            .key_context(CONTEXT)
            .size_full()
            .on_action(cx.listener(|this, _: &SaveFile, window, cx| this.save(window, cx)))

            .child(header)
            .when_some(self.save_error.clone(), |view, error| {
                view.child(
                    div()
                        .flex_none()
                        .px_3()
                        .py_1()
                        .border_b_1()
                        .border_color(border)
                        .text_color(danger)
                        .child(error),
                )
            })
            .child(div().flex_1().min_h_0().map(|body| {
                match &self.error {
                    Some(error) => body.p_3().text_color(muted).child(error.clone()),
                    // Read-only until the file's text is in, so nothing typed
                    // before is lost.
                    None => body.child(
                        Editor::new(&self.editor)
                            .readonly(self.saved.is_none())
                            .bordered(false)
                            .rounded_none()
                            .size_full(),
                    ),
                }
            }));
        // Lets UI tests find the file; inert in normal builds.
        gpui_kit::TestSupportExt::test_support(view)
    }

content.text:
The editor now keeps a minimum width of 80 columns of text, plus room for its line numbers. 91 of 92 tests pass, including a new one that shrinks the window to 300px and checks the editor stays at least 80 columns wide. The one failure is the palette test that was already failing. I haven't checked the result by eye in the running app.

- **How the width is worked out:** 80 times the width of one character in the editor's monospace font. On top of that goes room for the line numbers, which grows with the file's line count (at least 3 digits), plus about 6 columns for margins, fold icons and padding.
- **The split:** the file pane can't be dragged narrower than that. When a file opens, it takes half the width or the minimum, whichever is larger.
- **Narrow windows:** if the window is too narrow, the editor keeps its width and the edge beyond the window is cut off, rather than squeezing it. The task view beside it can also be squeezed to nothing in that case.
- **Accuracy:** the room for line numbers is an estimate. The editor library doesn't expose the true width of its line-number column, so the minimum may be a column or two more or less than exactly 80.

The change is in `src/file_view.rs`, plus the split's minimum in `src/prompt_mode.rs`.
